messages.content: How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?

function.name: calculate_vector_angle
function.description: Calculate the angle of a vector based on its X and Y components. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

X_component.description: The X component of the vector. This is a float type value.

Y_component.description: The Y component of the vector. This is a float type value.

use_degrees.description: If true, the result will be in degrees. If false, the result will be in radians. Default is false.

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How do I find the angle of the force for a given momentum?" They want to find angle of force given momentum. Likely they want to compute angle of force vector relative to something. They might need to use vector angle formula. They might need to use momentum vector and force vector relationship: Force is derivative of momentum: F = dp/dt. If momentum is known as a vector, the force direction is the same as the change in momentum direction. But maybe they want to compute angle between force and momentum. Use dot product: cosθ = (F·p)/(||F|| ||p||). So angle = arccos((F·p)/(||F|| ||p||)). Or if they have components of force and momentum, compute angle via arctan2. They might want to use the function calculate_vector_angle. Provide explanation. Also mention that if only magnitude of momentum and force known, cannot determine angle. Need components. Provide steps. Also mention using Python function. Provide example.
